Welcome. These pages hold **everything** you need for *Animal Tracking in
Conservation Biology*: slides, R practicals, datasets and further reading.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Everything here is public and permanent. Slides open in your browser — press
`F` for fullscreen, `S` for speaker notes, `E` for print/PDF view, `?` for all
shortcuts. Practicals are plain web pages you can work through at your own pace.
:::

## What this course is about

Biologging has changed what we can ask about animals. A collar that reports a
position every hour produces more raw observations in a week than a generation
of field naturalists could collect in a career. The bottleneck is no longer
data — it is **asking a well-posed question and knowing which analysis answers
it**.

The spine of the course is the **movement-ecology paradigm** (Nathan et al.
2008): every path is the joint outcome of an animal's internal state, its
motion capacity, its navigation capacity, and the external factors around it.
Tracking data record only the path. Every session is an attempt to reason back
from the path to those four components — and to be honest about how far the
data let us go.

Every concept is paired with code you run yourself, and three sessions use
**simulated animals whose true behaviour we know**, so you can see exactly how
each method succeeds and fails.

## The eight sessions

::: {.class-card}
[Session 1]{.topic-badge}

### Why animals move, and how we watch them
The movement-ecology paradigm; the ecological drivers of movement and their
trade-offs; tracking technologies and the 3–5% rule; how the fix interval
shapes the path you see.

→ [Slides](classes/class-01/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-01/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 2]{.topic-badge}

### Spatial data in R: the survival kit
Vector and raster, coordinate reference systems, choosing a projection for the
analysis, the `sf` and `terra` stack, and where environmental rasters come from.
Ends with a publication-quality map.

→ [Slides](classes/class-02/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-02/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 3]{.topic-badge}

### From fixes to trajectories
Positions are not paths. Location error, cleaning, bursts, gaps and
resampling; which analyses tolerate irregular sampling; annotating a track
with NDVI matched in time.

→ [Slides](classes/class-03/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-03/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 4]{.topic-badge}

### Quantifying movement
Net squared displacement, straightness, first-passage time; classifying
movement strategies; thresholds and behavioural change-point analysis — and
whether their answers survive a change of fix rate.

→ [Slides](classes/class-04/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-04/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 5]{.topic-badge}

### Movement models and simulation
Random, correlated, biased and Lévy walks. You write a simulator from scratch,
use it as a null model for real buffalo, and build the ground-truth animal for
the next two sessions.

→ [Slides](classes/class-05/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-05/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 6]{.topic-badge}

### Home ranges and space use
MCP, KDE, Brownian bridges and autocorrelated KDE on the same animal; variograms
and range residency; and a test of every estimator against a simulated animal
whose true home range we know.

→ [Slides](classes/class-06/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-06/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 7]{.topic-badge}

### Habitat selection on the move
Resource and step selection functions, integrated step selection, and relative
selection strength — fitted to New York fishers, and checked against a
simulated animal with a known selection coefficient.

→ [Slides](classes/class-07/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-07/exercise.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Session 8]{.topic-badge}

### Hidden Markov models and synthesis
Behavioural states, covariates on switching, how many states to believe; a
tour of the research frontier; and your mini-project pitches.

→ [Slides](classes/class-08/slides.qmd) · [Practical](classes/class-08/exercise.qmd)
:::

## Before the first session

1. Install R, RStudio and the course packages — see **[Software setup](setup.qmd)**.
2. Download the course project, which includes the **[datasets](data.qmd)**.
3. Bring a laptop. Every session has hands-on time.
